As can be seen in  Fig 1 , a clear disordinal interaction existed between fearful and happy conditions and participant group, such that patients with schizophrenia demonstrated reduced limbic activity in the bilateral striatum during the fearful face condition and increased striatal activity in the happy face condition.

value: Patients with schizophrenia had significantly reduced right striatal activity in response to fearful versus neutral faces compared to healthy individuals, and greater right orbitofrontal cortex activity when presented with happy versus neutral faces compared to controls.

Patients with schizophrenia demonstrated reduced limbic activity in the bilateral striatum during the fearful face condition and increased striatal activity in the happy face condition, whereas the opposite pattern was observed in healthy volunteers.

Individuals with schizophrenia also displayed significant prefrontal hyperactivity in the bilateral ventromedial prefrontal cortex and right orbitofrontal cortex during happy versus fearful trials compared to controls.

description.value: The Penn Emotion Recognition Test is a 40-item forced-choice measure of facial emotion perception. Participants matched an emotional label to happy, sad, fearful, angry, or neutral faces; accuracy and response time were used to assess emotion perception.

To examine the association between neural response to the effortful regulation of emotion and behavioral measures of emotion processing, emotion perception and emotional intelligence data were collected using the Penn Emotion Recognition Test [ 23 ] and the Mayer-Salovey-Caruso Emotional Intelligence Test (MSCEIT) [ 24 ].

description.value: The Mayer-Salovey-Caruso Emotional Intelligence Test is a 141-item performance-based measure of four domains of emotional intelligence. Participants solved emotional problems scored against normative responses rather than self-reporting emotional abilities.

spans.text: The MSCEIT is a 141-item performance-based measure of the four domains of emotional intelligence outlined by Salovey and Mayer [ 25 ].
